newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP steel cuts disappoint Australia govt.
newsitem.headline: BHP steel cuts disappoint Australia govt.

text.p: The Australian government said on Tuesday The Broken Hill Pty Ltd Co's decision to close steel plants was disappointing, but inevitable.
"No major company can afford to ignore the realities of its marketplace," Industry Minister John Moore said in a statement.
"The decision was widely expected and is consistent with the company's drive for competitiveness,
"However, it is regrettable that such changes have involved some closures."
"I am disappointed that BHP's planned restructure will involve the closure of facilities in Newcastle, Geelong and Sydney," Moore said.

"International trends have made it inevitable that BHP would have to substantially change its operations. BHP is a significant producer and exporter of steel by world standards and competitive pressures dictate continual improvements to reduce costs and improve efficiencies."

BHP announced earlier on Tuesday it would phase out steel-making at its major Newcastle plant, north of Sydney, by the end of 1999 and close its Geelong rod mill, in Victoria, and Sydney wire mill in 1999.
The cuts will see several thousand jobs go.
Moore said the Liberal-National government remained committed to the development of Australia's steel industry.

The year-old conservative administration would help the industry by improving the general business climate through reforms in transport, the waterfront and the labour market, he said. -- Canberra bureau 61-6 273-2730
